correctness.rationale: The four boundary sentences have ranks 1, 2, 3, 3. Nonzero idempotents are exactly e_ii, and a nonzero unit has one or two endpoint idempotents detectable by the stated atoms. Thus the covers in the last three sentences exist exactly for n <= 2, 3, 4, respectively; e_12 squares to zero when n >= 2, giving the first cutoff. For the tail, copy all coordinate equalities of the first two moves. Copy exactly on the last move whenever the total is at most five indices (including when the move introduces two fresh indices to a prefix with at most three). Otherwise the three edges have six distinct endpoints, and the last edge can reuse a previous row as its row while keeping a fresh column: row and column sets remain disjoint. The new edge is distinct, and every product of the three units, including squares, is zero. This preserves all multiplication and equality atoms including those with named zero, in either play direction. It proves the infinite tail, independently of any enumeration. Representation sizes are n^2+1. Independent replay: `python3 /workspace/branches/independent_checks.py 5` computes rank-three types directly from finite multiplication tables for n=1..6, returning five distinct initial types and equality at 5 and 6. The frozen three checkers and recorded outputs were inspected, not executed.
residual_risks: The independent computation is bounded. This audit concerns the specified relational signature and rank, not unrestricted sentences, other coefficient groups, extra symbols, or machine-formal certification.

value.rationale: A sharp logical cutoff for the whole matrix-unit family is useful for comparing finite semigroup presentations at bounded relational depth. It improves on the naive six-index copying bound and explains exactly which coordinate coincidence a rank-three observer cannot see. The four distinct lower boundaries and infinite tail make this more than a finite type tally.
